Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the NexMart Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Instructions for queuing questions will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Jordan Lee, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to NexMart's Second Quarter 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Elena Vasquez, CEO; Raj Patel, CFO; Maria Gonzalez, COO; and Chris Wong, CMO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Elena Vasquez, CEO of NexMart.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Jordan, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong second quarter performance, driven by robust growth in our seller services and value-added services revenue with impressive adoption rates boosting overall revenue, and significant progress in our international market expansion with key performance metrics exceeding expectations. We saw significant growth in key metrics like GMV up 14% year-over-year to $28.5 billion and active buyers reaching new highs.

Our focus remains on optimizing our take rate through strategic pricing adjustments and tighter promotional controls. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our new product launches like NovaAI Personalize and QuickNova, which we believe will significantly enhance conversion rates and customer retention. 

We are investing heavily in elevating seller performance metrics, including expanding our active seller base and increasing revenue per seller through targeted tools and programs.

Finally, we are committed to scaling these initiatives globally while maintaining high margins and platform stickiness.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Raj Patel, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Raj Patel:
Thank you, Elena. Our second quarter revenue was $6.5 billion, an increase of 32% year-over-year. Gross margin expanded to 45%, driven by higher take rates, improved fulfillment efficiencies, and the outsized contribution from our high-margin seller services segment. Operating expenses were $2.1 billion, representing 32% of revenue. Marketing spend increased 25% year-over-year to $850 million, focused on high-ROI channels like paid social and performance marketing in emerging markets, which helped drive customer acquisition while keeping CAC stable.

Our net income for the quarter was $850 million, or $1.25 per share. We ended the quarter with $4.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance of $28-30 billion in revenue and adjusted EBITDA margins of 25-27%.

Before we move on, let me dive deeper into some of our highest-margin and fastest-growing revenue streams, starting with seller services and value-added services. This segment now accounts for 28% of our total net revenue, up from 22% a year ago, and continues to be a key driver of our profitability and platform stickiness in this competitive e-commerce landscape. In the second quarter, it generated $1.82 billion in revenue, up 52% year-over-year and 18% quarter-over-quarter. This outpaced our overall revenue growth and contributed about 45% to our incremental revenue expansion. On a trailing 12-month basis, it's at $6.9 billion, representing a take rate of 2.8% on our record $245 billion in gross merchandise value. That's helping us close the gap with peers who report take rates around 3%, but we're gaining share through better seller economics.

Breaking it down by sub-segments, since diversification matters especially with advertising volatility from things like reduced ad spend amid inflation. Advertising revenues, the biggest piece at 48% or $875 million, grew 61% year-over-year. Sponsored products and display ads saw adoption jump to 72% among our top 10,000 sellers from 58% last year, thanks to our AI-powered NexBoost recommendation engine. It uses machine learning on 15 petabytes of real-time search and purchase data to deliver 28% higher click-through rates than generic tools, with deep integration into our storefront similar to how others have evolved their platforms.

Fulfillment and logistics services, 32% or $583 million up 55% year-over-year, benefited from NexFulfill now covering 85% of U.S. zip codes and expanding into 12 new centers in Southeast Asia. Adoption reached 68% for U.S. sellers over $1 million in annual GMV, up 12 points, as Prime-eligible sellers prioritize our two-day guarantees to win over the 65% of consumers who abandon carts without fast shipping.

Payments and financial services at 12% or $218 million, up 42%, scaled through NexPay processing 142 million transactions or $78 billion in total payment volume. Overall adoption is 54%, but 81% among SMBs in high-friction markets due to instant settlements and buy-now-pay-later options with partners like Affirm and Klarna.

The rest—analytics, software tools, and new things like carbon-neutral shipping—make up 8%, growing 70% as sellers embrace our upgraded Seller Central dashboard.

On adoption rates, which tell the real story, we track active sellers over 2.5 million globally, high-volume ones in the top 20% by GMV, and new ones from the last 12 months. Overall penetration hit 62% in Q2, up from 49% year-over-year, thanks to our cross-sell flywheel. High-volume sellers are at 89%, with 95% using at least two services, lifting their ARPU from $4,200 to $7,800 annually.

New sellers adopt at 71% within 90 days, driven by our Seller Success Program with freemium trials and AI chatbots for onboarding. This shines in fashion and electronics, where inventory turnover improved 22% for those using predictive demand forecasting.

Regionally, North America at 55% of segment revenue has 75% adoption, led by fulfillment amid rising USPS costs. APAC, 28% of revenue up 68% year-over-year, hits 82% in Indonesia and India through Shopee-like integrations handling 40 million parcels with J&T Express, though rural China faces data rules we're addressing with edge computing. EMEA and LATAM combined 17% at 55% adoption, with LATAM offsetting FX hits via 45% NexPay uptake against high local fees.

These rates amplify revenue impact—seller services have 78% gross margins, nearly triple marketplace ones, driving 62% of our adjusted EBITDA to $1.1 billion. Every 10-point adoption gain lifts GMV per seller 7%, creating a cycle of more SKUs up 18% year-over-year, more buyers, higher fees.

We're pushing adoption past 75% by year-end with NexAI Seller Suite in beta, using large language models on 500 million interactions for dynamic pricing, 34% chargeback reduction, and assortment recs. In a post-iOS14.5 world with ad attribution drops, our first-party data is a moat, scaled with Google Cloud. Full-year guide for this segment is $7.8-8.2 billion, 48-55% growth, turning us into a full-stack ecosystem.

Shifting to our take rate, which came in at 19.2% of GMV, up 110 basis points year-over-year from 18.1% and 40 basis points sequentially. This is our strongest expansion since late 2021, capturing an extra $285 million on $28.5 billion quarterly GMV up 14% despite softer discretionary demand. Our take rate—total revenue excluding ads and services divided by GMV—blends fixed commissions averaging 15-22%, fulfillment at 4-6%, and payments at 1.5-2.5%, resilient like peers but with our edge.

The uplift splits 60% to pricing and mix, 25% to promo discipline, 15% to technical and regional factors. Pricing added 65 basis points: we adjusted fees in top 80% GMV categories, blended commissions from 15.1% to 16.3%. Electronics at 28% GMV now 17% commissions without churn, NPS steady at 72 thanks to volume from ShopSphere Unlimited. Dynamic surcharges on 35% expedited orders added 20-30 basis points, powered by ML engine covering 60% listings using competitor data for 12% effective take rate lift.

Promos tightened 30 basis points: discounts down to 19% from 22%, capped in high-LTV areas, reducing leakage to 2.3% of GMV. We controlled flash sales for ROI over 2x and shifted to EMI preserving take rates, lifting AOV 8% to $145.

Mix shifts added 25 basis points: electronics and beauty at higher rates grew faster, private labels at 12% GMV and 25% take rates.

By region, North America 20.5% up 140 basis points, Europe 18.7% up 90 despite VAT, APAC 17.2% up 60 countering competition with tiered fees. We see 100-150 basis points more expansion to 20%+ by FY2025 via full AI rollout, ad inclusion, seller tools—capped to avoid churn, guided by A/B tests.

Now, on seller performance metrics, our ecosystem with over a million independents worldwide grew active sellers—those over $1,000 trailing 90-day GMV—to 1.28 million, up 28% year-over-year and 7% quarter-over-quarter. Net adds 112,000, churn down 300 basis points to 32% via AI churn prediction. Top-quartile at 18% of base do 45% GMV.

APAC led with 45% growth to 512,000 via UPI and partnerships; North America 8% to 420,000; EMEA 22% to 238,000; LATAM 62% to 110,000. SMBs 72% up 25%, mid-market 35%, enterprise 42%.

Revenue per seller hit $14,200, up 15% year-over-year, outpacing 9% GMV per seller growth to $112,000. Ads up 22% to $2,800 with 18% ROAS boost; fulfillment at 68%. Electronics up 28%, long-tail 12% via Boost program.

Investments like Seller AI Studio at 42% adoption, GraphQL v2, regional tools target 1.4 million actives and 14-16% revenue per seller growth in Q4.

Finally, our international expansion accounted for 32% of total GMV, up from 22%, with 48% year-over-year growth to $2.8 billion, outpacing domestic 18%. Revenue $285 million at 10% take rate, 28% of total. Active buyers 45 million MAUs up 62%, retention 78%, AOV $58 up 12%, fulfillment costs 14.2% down 180 basis points, CAC $22 down 15% with 4.2x LTV:CAC.

Europe 55% of int'l GMV at $1.54 billion up 52%, 8% share in fashion/electronics, Dutch/Spanish launches up 35% conversions, 22% margins. APAC 25% $700 million up 72%, India JV $250 million run-rate, SEA live-streaming up 150%. LATAM 12% $336 million up 38%, Pix integrations 40% conversions. MENA/Africa 8% $224 million up 110%, BNPL 45%.

Global One platform ensures uptime, GenAI boosts CTR 30%, logistics cuts 22%. $400 million CapEx to double capacity, targeting 40% GMV by YE25. On track for $12 billion int'l GMV FY24.

On new launches: NovaAI Personalize uplifts conversions 28% to 4.1%, AOV 15% to $145, $450 million GMV, NPS 78. QuickNova 1.2 million orders $180 million GMV, 14:32 delivery, NPS 82. NovaOwn $320 million at 22% margins, 4.6 stars. Services mix to 35%, retention up 14%.

These all tie together for strong execution.

Now I'll turn it over to Maria to discuss operations.

Maria Gonzalez:
Thanks, Raj. Operationally, we focused on scaling fulfillment capacity and optimizing supply chain resilience. Our shipping times improved by 25% year-over-year to an average of 1.8 days for Prime orders. Fulfillment costs declined 15% as a percentage of GMV to 12.5%, thanks to NexFulfill expansions and AI route optimization. We are implementing new robotics in 15 centers, reducing pick-and-pack times by 40%, which supports our quick delivery launches and international scaling.

Now I'll turn it over to Chris.

Chris Wong:
Thanks, Maria. From a marketing perspective, we saw strong results from our NexBoost sponsored ads campaign and TikTok Shop integrations, driving 62% MAU growth in APAC. Customer acquisition costs were $22, flat year-over-year despite scaling. Our brand awareness increased by 35% per Nielsen surveys, particularly in Europe and LATAM. We are focusing on personalized retargeting with GenAI to boost LTV while navigating rising ad costs.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for questions: Press star then 1 to queue, 2 to withdraw. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Smith:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Raj, can you expand on the seller services adoption trends, especially internationally, and how you're sustaining 50%+ growth there?

Raj Patel:
Thanks, Ben. Absolutely, adoption is the flywheel—62% overall, 82% in key APAC markets like Indonesia and India via strong logistics partnerships handling 40 million parcels. We're sustaining momentum with NexAI Suite for pricing and fraud tools, targeting 75% by year-end. Int'l high-volume sellers at 89% using multiple services, driving ARPU uplift. Full-year guide holds at 48-55% growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Laura Chen:
Great, thanks. Elena or Raj, on take rate expansion to 19.2%, what gives you confidence in another 100 basis points without hurting GMV growth, given competition?

Elena Vasquez:
Laura, good question. Raj covered the drivers—pricing discipline in electronics, promo tightening, mix shifts. Confidence comes from elasticity testing; our dynamic pricing engine shows no conversion drag, and seller NPS steady. Peers like us are balancing growth and margins effectively.

Raj Patel:
To add, we're capping at neutral levels, full AI rollout adds 50 basis points, and private labels contribute organically.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rivera with JPMorgan.

Mike Rivera:
Thanks. Maria, operations-wise, how are fulfillment improvements tying into international expansion, and any updates on new center ramps?

Maria Gonzalez:
Mike, spot on—our 12 new Southeast Asia centers cover 85% U.S. and growing int'l pin codes, driving 180 basis point fulfillment cost cuts globally. Berlin and Ontario ramps reduced Europe delivery to under 48 hours, supporting 52% GMV growth there. Robotics rollout next quarter accelerates this.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Kim with Barclays.

Sarah Kim:
Hi, team. Chris, marketing—how is customer feedback on new launches like QuickNova influencing spend allocation, and LTV impact?

Chris Wong:
Sarah, feedback is strong—NPS 82 on speed for QuickNova, with 65% week-one repeats boosting LTV:CAC to 4.2x. We're allocating more to TikTok in metros, tying AI personalization for 18% attach rate lift. Overall, cohort retention to six months up 14%.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Elena Vasquez for closing remarks.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
